annotations.text: As shipped, for comparison: five sections in one row grammar, a button or two on every row, and a friend flying right now reduced to a six-point dot and a dim word.

The pick, per Chris. The add box keeps its shipped style under ADD FRIEND. In this game, sent, the friends count and the ledger row are gone; incoming adds sit under RECEIVED. Friends are one head: a solid green dot and the zone (Team Battle, spelled as the catalog spells it) for a friend in a game, a hollow grey dot and nothing else for one who is off. No line is set all lower case, which is a design guideline now. The row press still raises the card, so join and unfriend live there for every input.

The invite banner, pinned above the rail: a door out of the game's own roster, for somebody who is not on the game at all. It reuses the ending key's share mechanics (the phone's share sheet, a copied link on a desktop, the key flipping to LINK COPIED), so the words name the outcome rather than the transport. Four wordings on the sheet beside this; the page wears C.

Round one: four directions beside the page as shipped, each keeping friends.md's three things (add somebody, see who is on, join in one press) and changing what the page looks like while it answers them. Chris picked a simpler line than any of them; the pick is on the first page.

A - Deck watch. The page reorders around now. A friend in a game gets the play page's live-row grammar: name large, game and clock and ground as stacks, the whole row lit, the whole row the join. Off friends are a plain roll, an add waiting on you is a hail band answered in place, the field folds behind the ADD key, and the ledger is one drill-in row at the foot. Cost: the field and the ledger are each a press further away.

B - The manifest. One aligned roster, every person one line: a mark carries the state, the WHERE column carries the game, at most one key rides a line. The five sections become a sort order, so the page scales to the hundred-edge cap without a second screen. Cost: the marks are a vocabulary nobody has been taught, and one-line rows leave no room for the ago words.

C - The crew wall. Friends drawn as crew rather than listed: a plaque each with the helmet mark from the pilot stop, lit in team blue when flying with the join on the plaque, gold-edged when they are asking. Cost: six plaques fill a screen, so it is thin at two friends and crowded at forty, and the plaque has no room for anything a row says in words.

D - By game. The page answers where instead of who: each zone holding a friend is a band with its clock and its names and the join on the band. Cost: nobody on, which is most opens, leaves a page of rolls under no band, and the band grammar re-draws the play page one tab over.
The empty state drawn in direction A: the field open with the completions the meta-layer answers from the first letter. Two thirds of accounts meet this page first, whichever direction wins.
